plan.summary: Add an in-memory DisagreementChecker, render an additive conflict section, and dual-wire Judge input while preserving old report compatibility.

steps.action: Add the DisagreementChecker persona definition in mirofish_lab/personas.py and implement in-memory diffing of the four reviewer outputs into topic/reviewers_for/reviewers_against/evidence entries.
steps.rollback: Redeploy the previous personas file and remove the DisagreementChecker persona.
steps.observability: Persona loads successfully; checker returns a list from review text only with no new persisted fields.

steps.action: Update pr-review-rehearsal/cli.py to run DisagreementChecker after parallel_run(reviewers, ...) and before Judge merge, using only the in-memory review outputs.
steps.rollback: Disable DisagreementChecker and restore the prior reviewer->judge flow.
steps.observability: Checker executes only after reviewer artifacts are recorded; no extra GitHub fetches occur.

steps.action: Extend the report serializer to insert a new additive 'Cross-reviewer conflicts' section between per-reviewer comments and implementer iteration, including an explicit empty-case message when no conflicts exist.
steps.rollback: Restore the previous report serializer and omit the conflict section.
steps.observability: Existing committed reports still parse; new section appears only as an additive block.

steps.action: Update the Judge prompt/input contract to accept an optional conflict list while preserving the old path when the list is absent.
steps.rollback: Redeploy the previous Judge prompt and drop the conflict payload.
steps.observability: Judge consumes conflict data when present and still works with legacy inputs.

steps.action: Add compatibility tests for legacy report parsing and for Judge behavior with and without the conflict list.
steps.rollback: Remove the new tests and revert to the previous test suite.
steps.observability: Tests confirm additive-only report shape and dual-support Judge input.

steps.action: Prepare release notes, consumer notice, support FAQ, and escalation ownership for the new additive section.
steps.rollback: Withdraw the notice and revert to the pre-change report template.
steps.observability: Notice is sent before release; support materials reference the new conflict section.

steps.action: Obtain security approval for the new conflict wording and the unchanged audit trail path.
steps.rollback: Revert to the previous report template with no conflict section.
steps.observability: Approved wording matches the report text; audit trail remains intact.

steps.action: Deploy behind the feature flag and canary on a small PR subset during business hours, outside incident and launch windows.
steps.rollback: Disable the feature flag and route all runs to the previous flow.
steps.observability: Canary error rate, parse failures, and conflict_detection_failure_rate stay within thresholds.

steps.action: Monitor the canary for 24 hours of successful runs and verify no parse failures before broadening rollout.
steps.rollback: Revert to the previous report schema and Judge prompt.
steps.observability: Track error rate, parse failures, and whether conflicts are surfaced correctly.

steps.action: Keep the feature flag as the immediate fallback and, if rollout slips or conflict detection fails, revert to judge-only flow.
steps.observability: Fallback remains available; judge-only path can be restored without schema changes.

open_questions: Who is the final release manager approver for the compatibility shim, if that shim is later needed?
Should the empty-case message be a fixed sentence or templated per reviewer set?
What exact wording should the customer notice and support FAQ use for the new conflict section?

conflicts.issue: SRE requires rollout only in a business-hours/no-incident window, while ProductPM also requires a release-notice/launch-window constraint. Resolved by sequencing notice and approvals before the business-hours canary, and treating both windows as rollout prerequisites.
SRE wants a canary on a small PR subset before broad enablement; ProductPM requires customer notice/support prep before release. Resolved by doing notice/FAQ first, then canary.

BackendOwner wants the Judge to accept an optional conflict list immediately, while ConsumerSubsystem requires dual-support for two release cycles. Resolved conservatively by making the new payload optional and preserving the old path during rollout.
